$comment: Shared project settings, committed. Personal overrides belong in
settings.local.json, which is gitignored and merges over this file.
No Stop hook here on purpose. A Stop hook that runs the unit suite would be
cheap and useful, but the checks that actually prove this project works --
eval.py and nis2/benchmark.py -- take minutes of local LLM time and would make
every turn unusable. Run those from /loop, which is bounded and asynchronous.
Add a Stop hook once there is a fast check that is worth blocking on.

$comment_pretooluse: Guardrail for the destructive operations specific to this project.
continueOnBlock lets Claude explain and pick another approach rather than

hooks.prompt:
Return {"ok": false, "reason": "blocked: <why>"} if this command does any of the following. Otherwise return {"ok": true}.

Irreversible git: force-pushes; pushes to main or master; resets, rebases or filter-branch on already-pushed history.

Secrets: reads, prints, copies or commits .env or any credential file; echoes a connection string or password unmasked.

MongoDB Atlas: drops a database, collection or search index; deletes documents; or rebuilds the vector index (main.py --rebuild-mongo). The free tier allows three search indexes and two are in use, so a dropped index may not be recreatable.

Baseline data: modifies nis2/ground_truth.json or eval_questions.json. These are the hand-labelled baselines the benchmarks score against; editing them to make a check pass destroys the only independent signal the project has.

Expensive rebuilds: main.py --rebuild-index or --rebuild-graph, each of which is minutes of local embedding.

Destructive filesystem: rm -rf outside a build, cache or temp directory.
